source.title_or_context: 15. 'What to do' and 'what not to do' messages from the Guidelines

table_assessment.assessment_notes: This summary table repeats recommendations appearing in earlier detailed tables from the same document (general, pulmonary-hypertension, aortic-disease, and valvular sections). It also mixes non-medication and medication rows, so suspected duplication and mixed content prevent readiness.

entities.surface_form: all women with known or suspected congenital or acquired cardiovascular and aortic disease

text_units.verbatim_text: Pre-pregnancy risk assessment and counselling is indicated in all women with known or suspected congenital or acquired cardiovascular and aortic disease.

normative_assertions.notes: The row directs high-risk patients to specialized-centre care by the pregnancy heart team.

text_units.verbatim_text: It is recommended to treat high risk patients in specialized centres by a multidisciplinary team: the pregnancy heart team.

entities.surface_form: any pregnant patient with unexplained or new cardiovascular signs or symptoms

text_units.verbatim_text: Echocardiography is recommended in any pregnant patient with unexplained or new cardiovascular signs or symptoms

normative_assertions.notes: Exceptions are referenced but not present in this fragment.

text_units.verbatim_text: Vaginal delivery is recommended as first choice in most patients; for most important exceptions see below.
Prophylactic antibiotic therapy to prevent endocarditis during delivery is not recommended.

entities.surface_form: very strict indications, optimal timing, and shielding of the foetus

header_path: Recommendations for pregnancy and pulmonary hypertension or congenital heart disease

text_units.verbatim_text: Right heart catheterization is recommended to confirm the diagnosis of PAH (group 1). This can be performed during pregnancy but with very strict indications, optimal timing, and shielding of the foetus.

header_path: Recommendations for pregnancy and pulmonary hypertension or congenital heart disease

normative_assertions.notes: No narrower allowed operation represents avoiding pregnancy.

text_units.verbatim_text: Pregnancy is not recommended in patients with PAH.

entities.surface_form: patients after Fontan operation and any associated complication

header_path: Recommendations for pregnancy and pulmonary hypertension or congenital heart disease

normative_assertions.notes: No narrower allowed operation represents avoiding pregnancy.

text_units.verbatim_text: Pregnancy is not recommended in patients after Fontan operation and any associated complication.

entities.surface_form: patients with a genetically proven aortic syndrome or known aortic disease

header_path: Recommendations for the management of aortic disease

text_units.verbatim_text: Imaging of the entire aorta (CT/MRI) is recommended before pregnancy in patients with a genetically proven aortic syndrome or known aortic disease.

entities.surface_form: woman with known aortic dilatation, (history of) dissection, or genetic predisposition for dissection

header_path: Recommendations for the management of aortic disease

normative_assertions.notes: Strict control entails monitoring/management of blood pressure.

text_units.verbatim_text: When a woman with known aortic dilatation, (history of) dissection, or genetic predisposition for dissection becomes pregnant, strict blood pressure control is recommended.

header_path: Recommendations for the management of aortic disease

normative_assertions.notes: Frequency depends on diagnosis/severity as stated parenthetically.

text_units.verbatim_text: Repeated echocardiographic imaging every 4–12 weeks (depending on the diagnosis and severity of dilatation) is recommended during pregnancy and 6 months post-partum in patients with ascending aorta dilatation.

entities.surface_form: all women with aortic dilatation or (history of) aortic dissection
experienced centre with a pregnancy heart team

header_path: Recommendations for the management of aortic disease

normative_assertions.notes: Delivery is directed to an experienced centre meeting the stated capability condition.

text_units.verbatim_text: It is recommended to deliver all women with aortic dilatation or (history of) aortic dissection in an experienced centre with a pregnancy heart team, where cardiothoracic surgery is available.

entities.surface_form: patients with an ascending aorta <40 mm

header_path: Recommendations for the management of aortic disease

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with an ascending aorta <40 mm, vaginal delivery is recommended.

header_path: Recommendations for the management of aortic disease

normative_assertions.notes: No narrower allowed operation represents avoiding pregnancy.

text_units.verbatim_text: Pregnancy is not recommended in patients with vascular Ehlers–Danlos syndrome.

entities.surface_form: patients with symptoms or pulmonary hypertension

header_path: Recommendations for the management of native valvular heart disease

text_units.verbatim_text: In patients with symptoms or pulmonary hypertension, restricted activities and beta-1-selective blockers are recommended.

header_path: Recommendations for the management of native valvular heart disease

text_units.verbatim_text: Diuretics are recommended when congestive symptoms persist despite beta-blockers.
